# package mms

```go
import "github.com/otfabric/go-mms"
```

Package mms implements the Manufacturing Message Specification (MMS) protocol — ISO 9506.

This package provides both client-side and server-side MMS implementations for communicating over the ISO/OSI stack (TPKT → COTP → Session → Presentation → ACSE → MMS).

The library is designed as a generic MMS implementation. It does not contain any IEC 61850 domain logic — that belongs in a separate higher-level package built on top of go-mms.

#### Client quick start {#hdr-Client_quick_start}

For real TCP connections, use the transport/iso subpackage:

	import "github.com/otfabric/go-mms/transport/iso"

	client, err := iso.Dial(ctx, "10.0.0.1:102",
	    iso.WithCalledTSelector([]byte{0x00, 0x01}),
	    iso.WithClientDialOptions(mms.DialOptions{
	        MMS: mms.MMSOptions{MaxPDUSize: 65000},
	    }),
	)

Or use [NewClient](#func-newclient) with an already-established [Transport](#type-transport):

	client, err := mms.NewClient(ctx, conn, mms.DialOptions{...})

Supported client services: [Client.Identify](#func-client-identify), [Client.Status](#func-client-status), [Client.Read](#func-client-read), [Client.ReadMultiple](#func-client-readmultiple), [Client.Write](#func-client-write), [Client.GetNameList](#func-client-getnamelist), [Client.GetNameListAll](#func-client-getnamelistall), [Client.GetVariableAccessAttributes](#func-client-getvariableaccessattributes), [Client.DefineNamedVariableList](#func-client-definenamedvariablelist), [Client.GetNamedVariableListAttributes](#func-client-getnamedvariablelistattributes), [Client.DeleteNamedVariableList](#func-client-deletenamedvariablelist), File services ([Client.FileOpen](#func-client-fileopen), [Client.FileRead](#func-client-fileread), [Client.FileClose](#func-client-fileclose), [Client.FileDirectory](#func-client-filedirectory), [Client.FileDelete](#func-client-filedelete), [Client.FileRename](#func-client-filerename), [Client.ObtainFile](#func-client-obtainfile)), Journal services ([Client.ReadJournalTimeRange](#func-client-readjournaltimerange), [Client.ReadJournalStartAfter](#func-client-readjournalstartafter)), and [Client.Close](#func-client-close).

Incoming InformationReport PDUs from the server are delivered via a registered callback:

	client.OnInformationReport(func(r *mms.InformationReportIndication) {
	    fmt.Println("report:", r.Values)
	})

	defer client.Close(ctx)

	result, _ := client.Read(ctx, mms.ReadRequest{
	    DomainID: "MyDomain",
	    ItemID:   "MyVariable",
	})
	fmt.Println(result.Value.Type())

#### Server quick start {#hdr-Server_quick_start}

Create a [Server](#type-server) with [NewServer](#func-newserver), register domains, variables, and handlers, then use [Server.ListenAndServe](#func-server-listenandserve) with a [TransportListener](#type-transportlistener) (or call [Server.Serve](#func-server-serve) per connection):

	import "github.com/otfabric/go-mms/transport/iso"

	srv := mms.NewServer(mms.ServerOptions{
	    MMS: mms.ServerMMSOptions{MaxPDUSize: 65000},
	})
	srv.HandleIdentify(func(ctx context.Context, _ mms.IdentifyRequest) (*mms.ServerIdentity, error) {
	    return &mms.ServerIdentity{Vendor: "My Corp", Model: "Device", Revision: "1.0"}, nil
	})
	srv.RegisterDomain("process")
	srv.RegisterVariable(mms.Variable{...})

	ln, _ := iso.Listen(":102")
	srv.ListenAndServe(ctx, ln) // owns ln; closes it on return

Supported server services: Identify, Status, GetNameList, GetVariableAccessAttributes, Read, Write, DefineNamedVariableList, GetNamedVariableListAttributes, DeleteNamedVariableList.

The server can send InformationReport to connected clients:

	for _, sc := range srv.Connections() {
	    sc.SendInformationReport(ctx, &mms.InformationReportRequest{
	        Variables: []mms.ObjectName{{Scope: mms.ObjectScopeDomain, Domain: "dom", ItemID: "temp"}},
	        Values:    []*mms.Value{mms.NewFloat(21.5)},
	    })
	}

Or broadcast to all connected clients:

	srv.Broadcast(ctx, &mms.InformationReportRequest{...})

#### Concurrency {#hdr-Concurrency}

A [Client](#type-client) is safe for concurrent use from multiple goroutines. Transport writes are serialized (sendMu) so encoded PDUs cannot interleave. Concurrent callers may still have multiple confirmed requests outstanding: after a send completes, the caller waits for its response while other goroutines may send. A background reader correlates confirmed responses by invoke ID and independently dispatches unconfirmed PDUs (InformationReport) to the registered handler.

Negotiated MaxOutstandingCalling / MaxOutstandingCalled (see [Client.Negotiated](#func-client-negotiated)) are proposed during Initiate and exposed for inspection, but are not enforced as a runtime pending-request limit today. Callers that need back-pressure should limit concurrency themselves. Details: LIMITS.md, KNOWN\_LIMITATIONS.md, RACE\_NOTES.md.

A [Server](#type-server) is safe for concurrent use. Each [Server.Serve](#func-server-serve) call handles one association; multiple connections are served in parallel by calling Serve in separate goroutines. Within a single connection, confirmed requests are handled serially. Unconfirmed PDUs (InformationReport) can be sent concurrently via [ServerConn](#type-serverconn).

#### Supported services {#hdr-Supported_services}

Client services:

  - Identify, Status
  - Read, ReadMultiple, Write
  - GetNameList, GetNameListAll
  - GetVariableAccessAttributes
  - DefineNamedVariableList, GetNamedVariableListAttributes, DeleteNamedVariableList
  - InformationReport (receive via [Client.OnInformationReport](#func-client-oninformationreport))
  - File services (Open/Read/Close/Directory/Delete/Rename/ObtainFile)
  - Journal services (ReadJournal by time range or start-after)

Server services:

  - Identify, Status
  - Read, Write
  - GetNameList (Domain+VMD scope, NamedVariable+Domain/VMD scope, NamedVariableList+Domain/VMD scope)
  - GetVariableAccessAttributes
  - DefineNamedVariableList, GetNamedVariableListAttributes, DeleteNamedVariableList
  - InformationReport (send via [ServerConn.SendInformationReport](#func-serverconn-sendinformationreport) or [Server.Broadcast](#func-server-broadcast))
  - File services (via [FileProvider](#type-fileprovider))
  - Journal services (via [JournalProvider](#type-journalprovider))

Named variable list services (DefineNamedVariableList, GetNamedVariableListAttributes, DeleteNamedVariableList) are supported on both client and server.

#### Transport {#hdr-Transport}

The transport/iso subpackage provides real TCP+TPKT+COTP transport. It offers DialTCP (transport-only), Dial (transport + MMS client), and Listen (server-side accept with COTP handshake).

For testing or custom transports, implement [Transport](#type-transport) directly and pass it to [NewClient](#func-newclient) or [Server.Serve](#func-server-serve).

Out of scope:

  - IEC 61850 object-model or naming helpers

#### Server GetNameList combinations {#hdr-Server_GetNameList_combinations}

The server supports these ObjectClass+Scope combinations:

  - ObjectClassDomain + ObjectScopeVMD → list domain names
  - ObjectClassNamedVariable + ObjectScopeDomain → list variables in a domain
  - ObjectClassNamedVariable + ObjectScopeVMD → list VMD-scoped variables
  - ObjectClassNamedVariableList + ObjectScopeDomain → list NVLs in a domain
  - ObjectClassNamedVariableList + ObjectScopeVMD → list VMD-scoped NVLs

All other combinations return a service error.

#### Value ownership {#hdr-Value_ownership}

[Value](#type-value) instances are safe to store and pass between goroutines. Constructors (e.g. [NewOctetString](#func-newoctetstring), [NewArray](#func-newarray)) defensively copy byte slices and element slices so the caller retains no aliased references. Accessors that return byte slices (e.g. [Value.OctetString](#func-value-octetstring)) likewise return copies. For composite values (arrays, structures), the element slice header is copied but child [\*Value](#type-value) pointers are shared; use [Value.Clone](#func-value-clone) when full deep-copy semantics are required.

#### Error handling {#hdr-Error_handling}

Errors fall into several categories:

  - Sentinel errors (ErrClosed, ErrConnectionRejected, etc.) can be checked with [errors.Is](https://pkg.go.dev/errors#Is).
  - Typed errors ([ServiceError](#type-serviceerror), [DataAccessError](#type-dataaccesserror), [ProtocolError](#type-protocolerror), [AuthenticationError](#type-authenticationerror)) can be extracted with [errors.As](https://pkg.go.dev/errors#As) and carry structured detail (error class, code, phase, etc.).
  - Per-variable data access errors are returned as [\*DataAccessError](#type-dataaccesserror) from single-variable helpers ([Client.Read](#func-client-read), [Client.Write](#func-client-write)) and as [DataAccessErrorCode](#type-dataaccesserrorcode) fields in multi-variable results ([AccessResult](#type-accessresult), [WriteAccessResult](#type-writeaccessresult)).

#### Architecture {#hdr-Architecture}

The public API exposes MMS concepts only. All ISO stack internals (session, presentation, ACSE) are handled transparently. Transport is delegated to the transport/iso subpackage, which uses otfabric/go-tpkt and otfabric/go-cotp internally.

## Functions

### func IsRetryable

```go
func IsRetryable(err error) bool
```

IsRetryable is the default [RetryPolicy.Retryable](#func-retrypolicy-retryable) classification. It returns false for errors that another attempt cannot fix — context cancellation, invalid arguments, authentication failures, and associations rejected by the peer — and true for everything else (refused or dropped connections, timeouts including a per-attempt context deadline, protocol failures during the handshake). [Retry](#func-retry) stops on its own when its context is done.

### func Retry

```go
func Retry(ctx context.Context, p RetryPolicy, fn func(ctx context.Context) error) error
```

Retry calls fn until it succeeds, the policy gives up, or ctx is done. Each call gets ctx. Between attempts Retry waits according to p; a cancelled ctx interrupts the wait. It returns nil on success, otherwise the last error from fn (or ctx's error, joined with the last error, when ctx ended the retries).

A typical reconnect loop:

	client, err := ... // first dial
	for {
	    <-client.Done()
	    err = mms.Retry(ctx, mms.DefaultRetryPolicy(), func(ctx context.Context) error {
	        c, err := iso.Dial(ctx, addr)
	        if err == nil {
	            client = c
	        }
	        return err
	    })
	    if err != nil {
	        return err
	    }
	}

### type AuthContext

```go
type AuthContext struct {
	// Mechanism is the normalized authentication mechanism.
	//
	// [AuthMechanismTLSCertificate] is transport-derived: the server
	// infers it when no ACSE mechanism is present but the TLS transport
	// provides a peer certificate. It does not correspond to an ACSE
	// mechanism-name OID; [MechanismOID] will be nil in that case.
	Mechanism AuthMechanism

	// MechanismOID is the ACSE mechanism OID from the AARQ, decoded
	// from BER into a structured OID. Nil when no mechanism was
	// presented. For password auth this is {2, 2, 3, 1}.
	MechanismOID asn1.ObjectIdentifier

	// Password is the ACSE password bytes, populated when Mechanism
	// is [AuthMechanismACSEPassword]. This is a defensive copy; the
	// caller's original slice is not shared.
	Password []byte

	// CallingApplication is the calling AP-title and AE-qualifier
	// from the AARQ. Nil when not present. This is the primary
	// association identity for access control alongside the mechanism.
	CallingApplication *ApplicationReference

	// PeerCertificate is the leaf TLS peer certificate, populated when
	// the transport is TLS-secured and the peer presented a certificate.
	// Nil when TLS is not active or no peer certificate was provided.
	PeerCertificate *x509.Certificate

	// RemoteAddr is the network address of the remote peer. Nil when
	// the transport does not expose address information.
	RemoteAddr net.Addr
}
```

AuthContext holds all authentication-relevant information for an incoming association. It is passed to the [Authenticator](#type-authenticator) callback during association establishment.

Fields are populated from the ACSE AARQ and, where available, from TLS transport state. Absent optional fields are nil/zero.

### type AuthMechanism

```go
type AuthMechanism int
```

AuthMechanism identifies the authentication mechanism used during association establishment.

The zero value is AuthMechanismUnknown. It indicates that an authentication mechanism was presented but could not be classified. Absence of authentication is represented by AuthMechanismNone.

```go
const (
	// AuthMechanismUnknown indicates the peer presented an ACSE
	// authentication mechanism that this library does not recognize.
	// The raw OID is available in [AuthContext].MechanismOID.
	AuthMechanismUnknown AuthMechanism = iota

	// AuthMechanismNone indicates no authentication was provided —
	// no ACSE auth fields and no TLS peer certificate.
	AuthMechanismNone

	// AuthMechanismACSEPassword indicates ACSE password authentication
	// (mechanism OID 2.2.3.1). The password is available in
	// [AuthContext].Password.
	//
	// SECURITY: ACSE password auth transmits credentials inside the
	// AARQ. Without TLS, the password travels in the clear. Password
	// auth should normally be combined with TLS transport security.
	AuthMechanismACSEPassword

	// AuthMechanismTLSCertificate indicates TLS-level peer certificate
	// authentication. This mechanism is inferred when no ACSE
	// authentication is present but the TLS transport provides peer
	// certificates. The leaf certificate is available in
	// [AuthContext].PeerCertificate.
	AuthMechanismTLSCertificate
)
```

### type Authenticator

```go
type Authenticator func(ctx context.Context, auth *AuthContext) (AuthResult, error)
```

Authenticator is a server callback invoked during association establishment to decide whether to accept or reject the peer.

It receives a [context.Context](https://pkg.go.dev/context#Context) (with the Serve deadline if any) and the [AuthContext](#type-authcontext) describing the association's authentication material.

Return an [AuthResult](#type-authresult) with Accept=true to accept, or Accept=false to reject. The error return is reserved for internal failures (e.g. backend lookup errors); returning a non-nil error also rejects the association.

If not set on [ServerOptions](#type-serveroptions), all associations are accepted with a nil token.

Example authenticator for ACSE password policy:

	func myAuth(_ context.Context, auth *mms.AuthContext) (mms.AuthResult, error) {
	    if auth.Mechanism != mms.AuthMechanismACSEPassword {
	        return mms.AuthResult{}, nil // reject: wrong mechanism
	    }
	    if !bytes.Equal(auth.Password, []byte("secret")) {
	        return mms.AuthResult{}, nil // reject: wrong password
	    }
	    return mms.AuthResult{Accept: true, Token: "operator"}, nil
	}

Example authenticator for TLS client certificate policy:

	func tlsAuth(_ context.Context, auth *mms.AuthContext) (mms.AuthResult, error) {
	    if auth.PeerCertificate == nil {
	        return mms.AuthResult{}, nil // reject: no peer cert
	    }
	    cn := auth.PeerCertificate.Subject.CommonName
	    if !isAllowedOperator(cn) {
	        return mms.AuthResult{}, nil
	    }
	    return mms.AuthResult{Accept: true, Token: cn}, nil
	}

Example authenticator for AP-title policy:

	func apTitleAuth(_ context.Context, auth *mms.AuthContext) (mms.AuthResult, error) {
	    if auth.CallingApplication == nil {
	        return mms.AuthResult{}, nil
	    }
	    if !auth.CallingApplication.APTitle.Equal(allowedTitle) {
	        return mms.AuthResult{}, nil
	    }
	    return mms.AuthResult{Accept: true}, nil
	}

### type Client

```go
type Client struct {

	// serializes writes to transport

	// closed when reader loop exits
	// why the reader loop exited; guarded by mu
	// receives signal when ConcludeResponse arrives

	// Negotiated parameters from MMS Initiate handshake.

}
```

Client is an MMS client connection to a remote MMS server.

A Client is created via [NewClient](#func-newclient) (or the convenience iso.Dial from the transport/iso subpackage) and must be closed with [Client.Close](#func-client-close) when no longer needed.

Close is idempotent: calling it multiple times is safe and subsequent calls return nil.

Concurrency: the Client serializes transport writes (one PDU write at a time). Concurrent callers may have multiple confirmed requests outstanding; a background reader correlates responses by invoke ID and delivers unconfirmed PDUs (InformationReport) to registered handlers. Negotiated outstanding-request limits are not enforced at runtime (see package doc Concurrency).

#### func NewClient

```go
func NewClient(ctx context.Context, conn Transport, opts DialOptions) (*Client, error)
```

NewClient creates a Client using an already-established [Transport](#type-transport) connection. This is the low-level entry point for creating clients with custom or pre-established transports.

NewClient performs the full ISO upper-layer association and MMS Initiate handshake over the provided transport.

#### func (Client) Abort

```go
func (c *Client) Abort(ctx context.Context) error
```

Abort performs a hard, immediate association abort without the graceful ConcludeRequest/ConcludeResponse exchange. Use this for protocol desync recovery, emergency teardown, or test tooling.

After Abort returns, the Client is closed and all pending requests are cancelled with ErrClosed.

The ABRT PDU is sent best-effort and bounded by ctx; the transport is closed even when the send fails or ctx expires.

#### func (Client) Close

```go
func (c *Client) Close(ctx context.Context) error
```

Close performs an orderly shutdown of the MMS connection (Conclude). Use [Client.Abort](#func-client-abort) for an immediate one.

Shutdown sequence:

 1. Marks the client as closed — all new service calls return ErrClosed.
 2. Cancels all pending confirmed requests with ErrClosed.
 3. Sends a ConcludeRequest and waits for the ConcludeResponse.
 4. Stops the background reader loop and closes the transport.

This is NOT a graceful drain: pending requests are aborted immediately and their callers receive ErrClosed. Confirmed responses that arrive during the shutdown window (after CancelAll but before the reader exits) are discarded as unknown invoke IDs.

Close is idempotent: the first call performs the conclude handshake; subsequent calls return nil.

Done returns a channel that is closed when the association has ended: after [Client.Close](#func-client-close) or [Client.Abort](#func-client-abort), when the peer concludes, releases or aborts, or when the connection is lost or fails to decode. Use it to detect a lost association and reconnect (see [Retry](#func-retry)).

#### func (Client) GetNameListAll

```go

```

GetNameListAll retrieves all named objects by automatically handling continuation. It repeatedly calls [Client.GetNameList](#func-client-getnamelist) until MoreFollows is false.

As a safety measure, GetNameListAll detects stalled pagination (where the server repeats the same continuation token) and returns an error.

Note: this method accumulates all names in memory. For servers with very large name lists, prefer using [Client.GetNameList](#func-client-getnamelist) directly with explicit pagination control.

```go
type DataAccessError struct {

```


### type DataAccessErrorCode

```go
type DataAccessErrorCode int
```

DataAccessErrorCode represents per-variable access errors returned by MMS read/write operations.

The values match the MMS ASN.1 data-access-error ENUMERATED wire encoding (ISO 9506-2). DataAccessErrorNone (-1) is a Go-internal sentinel meaning "no error"; it is never transmitted on the wire.

```go
const (
	// DataAccessErrorNone is the no-error sentinel. A value of -1 is
	// never encoded on the wire; it indicates the absence of an error in
	// AccessResult and WriteAccessResult fields.
	DataAccessErrorNone DataAccessErrorCode = -1

	// Wire values 0–11 match the MMS data-access-error ENUMERATED (ISO 9506-2).
	DataAccessErrorObjectInvalidated           DataAccessErrorCode = 0
	DataAccessErrorHardwareFault               DataAccessErrorCode = 1
	DataAccessErrorTemporarilyUnavailable      DataAccessErrorCode = 2
	DataAccessErrorObjectAccessDenied          DataAccessErrorCode = 3
	DataAccessErrorObjectUndefined             DataAccessErrorCode = 4
	DataAccessErrorInvalidAddress              DataAccessErrorCode = 5
	DataAccessErrorTypeUnsupported             DataAccessErrorCode = 6
	DataAccessErrorTypeInconsistent            DataAccessErrorCode = 7
	DataAccessErrorObjectAttributeInconsistent DataAccessErrorCode = 8
	DataAccessErrorObjectAccessUnsupported     DataAccessErrorCode = 9
	DataAccessErrorObjectNonExistent           DataAccessErrorCode = 10
	DataAccessErrorObjectValueInvalid          DataAccessErrorCode = 11
)
```

#### func (DataAccessErrorCode) String

```go
func (c DataAccessErrorCode) String() string
```

String returns the human-readable name of the DataAccessErrorCode.

### type DialOptions

```go
type DialOptions struct {
	Transport TransportOptions
	ISO       ISOOptions
	MMS       MMSOptions

	// Logger, when non-nil, enables structured MMS logging. When nil
	// (default), a discard handler is used (zero overhead). Lifecycle
	// events at Info; request/response summaries at Debug.
	// Does not configure transport/iso logging — use iso.WithLogger
	// separately (see OBSERVABILITY.md).
	Logger *slog.Logger

	// RawHook, when non-nil, is called for every raw ISO upper-layer
	// payload sent to or received from the transport. direction is
	// [RawHookSend] ("send") or [RawHookRecv] ("recv"). raw contains the
	// session SPDU bytes (which embed presentation, ACSE, and MMS data).
	//
	// This hook operates at the COTP user-data level, not at the MMS PDU
	// level specifically. It is intended for packet capture and replay
	// tooling.
	RawHook func(direction string, raw []byte)

	// Metrics, when non-nil, receives request and connection events (see
	// [Metrics]). Nil means no metrics.
	Metrics Metrics

	// RequestTimeout, when positive, bounds every confirmed request whose
	// context has no earlier deadline. A request that times out fails with
	// an error matching both [ErrInvokeTimeout] and
	// [context.DeadlineExceeded]. Zero means no default timeout: requests
	// wait until their context is done or the connection is lost.
	RequestTimeout time.Duration

	// AllowedServices, when non-nil, lists the confirmed services the
	// client may send. A request for any other service is refused before
	// it reaches the transport: nothing is sent, and the call returns an
	// error matching [ErrServiceNotAllowed] (the [Metrics] request event
	// carries the same error). Nil allows every service; an empty non-nil
	// slice refuses every confirmed request. Association control
	// (Initiate, Conclude, Abort) is not a confirmed service and is never
	// refused. Use it to make a client read-only, for example
	// {ServiceIdentify, ServiceStatus, ServiceGetNameList, ServiceRead,
	// ServiceGetVariableAccessAttributes, ServiceGetNamedVariableListAttributes}.
	AllowedServices []Service
}
```

DialOptions configures the MMS client connection.

Options are grouped by protocol layer to avoid a flat, cross-layer catch-all struct. The exact grouping may evolve, but separation by responsibility is maintained.

### type FileProvider

```go
type FileProvider interface {
	// List returns entries matching the request's FileSpec, with
	// optional pagination via ContinueAfter and MaxEntries.
	List(ctx context.Context, req FileListRequest) (*FileListResult, error)

	Open(ctx context.Context, path string) (FileHandle, FileAttributes, error)

	// Read returns the next chunk of data from handle, up to maxBytes.
	// On the final (or only) chunk the implementation must return
	// moreFollows=false with a nil error. Returning io.EOF is treated
	// as a provider error; use moreFollows=false to signal end-of-file.
	Read(ctx context.Context, handle FileHandle, maxBytes int) (data []byte, moreFollows bool, err error)

	Close(ctx context.Context, handle FileHandle) error
	Delete(ctx context.Context, path string) error

	// Rename renames a file. Implementations should return
	// [fs.ErrNotExist] if the source does not exist.
	Rename(ctx context.Context, currentName, newName string) error

	// ObtainFile copies sourceFile to destinationFile on the server.
	// Implementations may return [fs.ErrNotExist] if the source does
	// not exist, or [ErrFileAccessDenied] for permission errors.
	// Returning nil indicates success.
	ObtainFile(ctx context.Context, sourceFile, destinationFile string) error
}
```

FileProvider is the server-side abstraction for MMS file services. Implementations back the FileOpen/Read/Close/Delete/Directory protocol services. The server does not access the filesystem directly; all I/O goes through this interface.

Provider errors are mapped to MMS service errors by the server:

  - [fs.ErrNotExist](https://pkg.go.dev/io/fs#ErrNotExist) → file-non-existent
  - [fs.ErrPermission](https://pkg.go.dev/io/fs#ErrPermission) or ErrFileAccessDenied → file-access-denied
  - all other errors → other


### type ISOOptions

```go
type ISOOptions struct {
	LocalAPTitle      APTitle
	RemoteAPTitle     APTitle
	LocalAEQualifier  int
	RemoteAEQualifier int
	LocalPSelector    []byte
	RemotePSelector   []byte
	LocalSSelector    []byte
	RemoteSSelector   []byte

	// Password, when non-nil, includes ACSE password authentication
	// in the association request (AARQ). The server must be configured
	// to accept password-based authentication.
	//
	// SECURITY: The password is embedded in the AARQ PDU and transmitted
	// as part of the ISO upper-layer association request. Without TLS,
	// the password travels in the clear over the wire — this is
	// plaintext-equivalent and offers no confidentiality against network
	// observers. ACSE password authentication should normally be
	// combined with TLS transport security ([transport/iso.WithTLSConfig]).
	// The library does not enforce this combination; it is the caller's
	// responsibility to ensure adequate transport security.
	//
	// The slice is copied internally; the caller may reuse or modify
	// the original after passing it.
	Password []byte
}
```

ISOOptions configures the ISO upper layers (session, presentation, ACSE).

A client sends the addressing that libiec61850 and most IEC 61850 clients send, and that IEDs are configured for, unless set otherwise (IEC 61850-8-1 Table 132 makes these SCL address parameters but mandates no value):

	S-selector      00 01 (calling and called)
	P-selector      00 00 00 01 (calling and called)
	AP-title        1.1.1.999 (calling), 1.1.1.999.1 (called)
	AE-qualifier    12 (calling and called)

A nil selector or AP-title takes the default; a non-nil empty one is omitted from the request. An AE-qualifier is sent only with its AP-title: it is 12 when the AP-title is the default and the qualifier is zero, and the configured value otherwise.

### type JournalProvider

```go
type JournalProvider interface {
	// ListJournals returns journal names available in the given domain.
	// Currently only domain-scoped journals are supported in the
	// server dispatch (ObjectClassJournal + ScopeDomain).
	ListJournals(ctx context.Context, domain string) ([]string, error)

	// ReadTimeRange returns journal entries within [start, stop].
	// maxEntries is a hint; the provider may return fewer entries.
	// Set [JournalResult.MoreFollows] to true if more entries are
	// available beyond those returned.
	ReadTimeRange(ctx context.Context, domain, journal string,
		start, stop time.Time, maxEntries int) (*JournalResult, error)

	// ReadStartAfter returns journal entries starting after the given
	// cursor (afterID, afterTime). Use the last entry's EntryID and
	// OccurrenceTime from a previous result to page through data.
	// maxEntries is a hint; the provider may return fewer entries.
	// Set [JournalResult.MoreFollows] to true if more entries remain.
	ReadStartAfter(ctx context.Context, domain, journal string,
		afterID []byte, afterTime time.Time, maxEntries int) (*JournalResult, error)
}
```

JournalProvider is implemented by applications to back journal services. The server calls these methods in response to ReadJournal requests.

The provider methods use the same domain types as the client API ([JournalEntry](#type-journalentry), [JournalVariable](#type-journalvariable), [JournalResult](#type-journalresult)). This is an intentional design choice: journal entries have a fixed structure defined by the MMS protocol, so a single set of types serves both sides without loss of fidelity.

#### Ordering contract {#hdr-Ordering_contract}

Entries returned by ReadTimeRange and ReadStartAfter MUST be in ascending chronological order by OccurrenceTime. When multiple entries share the same OccurrenceTime, they MUST be in a stable, deterministic order (e.g. by EntryID). ReadStartAfter semantics depend on this ordering: the server sends the client the last entry's (OccurrenceTime, EntryID) as the continuation cursor.

#### Pagination {#hdr-Pagination}

The provider MAY return fewer than maxEntries entries. When [JournalResult.MoreFollows](#func-journalresult-morefollows) is true, the caller should issue a ReadStartAfter request using the last returned entry's OccurrenceTime and EntryID to retrieve the next page. The server passes defaultMaxJournalEntries (currently 100) as maxEntries.

#### Error mapping {#hdr-Error_mapping}

If the provider returns [fs.ErrNotExist](https://pkg.go.dev/io/fs#ErrNotExist), the server maps it to MMS error class "access" (7), code "object-non-existent" (0). If the provider returns [fs.ErrPermission](https://pkg.go.dev/io/fs#ErrPermission) or ErrFileAccessDenied, the server maps it to "access" (7), code "object-access-denied" (1). All other errors are mapped to "access" (7), code "other" (0).

### type JournalResult

```go
type JournalResult struct {
	Entries     []JournalEntry
	MoreFollows bool
}
```

JournalResult holds the result of a ReadJournal call, including continuation state for paging. When MoreFollows is true, use [Client.ReadJournalStartAfter](#func-client-readjournalstartafter) with the last entry's OccurrenceTime and EntryID to retrieve the next page.

### type Metrics

```go
type Metrics interface {
	// ObserveRequest is called once per confirmed service request: by the
	// client when the response (or error) is delivered to the caller, and
	// by the server when the response (or error PDU) has been sent.
	ObserveRequest(RequestEvent)

	// ObserveConnection is called when an association is established,
	// rejected or ends.
	ObserveConnection(ConnectionEvent)
}
```

Metrics receives operational events from a [Client](#type-client) or [Server](#type-server). Set it with [DialOptions.Metrics](#func-dialoptions-metrics) or [ServerOptions.Metrics](#func-serveroptions-metrics); when nil, events are dropped ([NopMetrics](#type-nopmetrics)).

go-mms has no metrics dependency. Adapt this interface to the metrics library of your choice (Prometheus, OpenTelemetry, expvar, ...); see OBSERVABILITY.md for a Prometheus example.

Methods are called synchronously on the goroutine that completed the operation, so implementations must be safe for concurrent use and should return quickly. Embed [NopMetrics](#type-nopmetrics) in your implementation so that methods added to this interface in later minor releases do not break your build.

### type RetryPolicy

```go
type RetryPolicy struct {
	// MaxAttempts is the total number of attempts, including the first.
	// 0 and 1 mean a single attempt; a negative value retries until the
	// context is done.
	MaxAttempts int

	// InitialBackoff is the delay before the second attempt. Zero means
	// 100ms.
	InitialBackoff time.Duration

	// MaxBackoff caps the delay between attempts. Zero means 30s.
	MaxBackoff time.Duration

	// Multiplier is the factor applied to the delay after each attempt.
	// Values below 1 mean 2.
	Multiplier float64

	// Jitter randomizes each delay by up to this fraction, downwards: a
	// delay d becomes a random value in [d*(1-Jitter), d]. It must be in
	// [0, 1]; 0 disables jitter. Jitter spreads reconnect storms when
	// many clients lose the same server.
	Jitter float64

	// Retryable reports whether err is worth another attempt. Nil means
	// [IsRetryable].
	Retryable func(err error) bool

	// OnRetry, when non-nil, is called before each wait with the 1-based
	// number of the attempt that failed, its error and the delay before
	// the next attempt. Use it for logging or metrics.
	OnRetry func(attempt int, err error, delay time.Duration)
}
```

RetryPolicy configures retries with exponential backoff and jitter. It is used by transport/iso.WithRetry for dialing, and by [Retry](#func-retry) for any operation such as re-establishing a lost association.

The zero value performs a single attempt (no retries). Use [DefaultRetryPolicy](#func-defaultretrypolicy) for sensible defaults.

#### func DefaultRetryPolicy

```go
func DefaultRetryPolicy() RetryPolicy
```

DefaultRetryPolicy returns a policy of 5 attempts with delays starting at 200ms, doubling up to 10s, with 20% jitter.

#### func (RetryPolicy) Backoff

```go
func (p RetryPolicy) Backoff(attempt int) time.Duration
```

Backoff returns the delay after the given failed attempt (1-based), before jitter.

### type Server

```go
type Server struct {
	// contains filtered or unexported fields
}
```

Server is a generic MMS server that accepts associations and serves confirmed MMS services via registered handlers and a variable registry.

Create a Server with [NewServer](#func-newserver), register handlers and variables, then call [Server.Serve](#func-server-serve) to handle a single transport connection or [Server.ListenAndServe](#func-server-listenandserve) with a [TransportListener](#type-transportlistener) for an accept loop.

Active server connections can be iterated via [Server.Connections](#func-server-connections) and used to send unconfirmed PDUs such as InformationReport.

#### func NewServer

```go
func NewServer(opts ServerOptions) *Server
```

NewServer creates a new MMS server with the given options.

#### func (Server) Broadcast

```go
func (s *Server) Broadcast(ctx context.Context, req *InformationReportRequest) error
```

Broadcast sends an InformationReport to all currently connected clients. Errors from individual connections are logged but do not stop delivery to remaining connections.

#### func (Server) Connections

```go
func (s *Server) Connections() []*ServerConn
```

Connections returns a snapshot of currently active server connections. Each [ServerConn](#type-serverconn) can be used to send unsolicited PDUs.

#### func (Server) HandleIdentify

```go
func (s *Server) HandleIdentify(h func(context.Context, IdentifyRequest) (*ServerIdentity, error))
```

HandleIdentify registers a handler for the MMS Identify service.

#### func (Server) HandleStatus

```go
func (s *Server) HandleStatus(h func(context.Context, StatusRequest) (*ServerStatus, error))
```

HandleStatus registers a handler for the MMS Status service.

#### func (Server) ListenAndServe

```go
func (s *Server) ListenAndServe(ctx context.Context, ln TransportListener) error
```

ListenAndServe accepts connections from the given listener and serves each one in a new goroutine. It blocks until the context is cancelled or the listener returns a fatal (non-temporary) error.

Ownership:

  - ListenAndServe takes ownership of the listener and closes it on return. The caller must not close the listener separately.
  - Each accepted transport is closed automatically when its Serve goroutine finishes (via deferred Close).

Each accepted connection is handled by [Server.Serve](#func-server-serve) in its own goroutine. Connection-level serve errors are logged but do not stop the accept loop. Temporary accept errors (e.g. transient network issues) are logged and retried. Fatal accept errors stop the server.

#### func (Server) RegisterDomain

```go
func (s *Server) RegisterDomain(name string) error
```

RegisterDomain adds a domain to the server's MMS object model.

#### func (Server) RegisterNamedVariableList

```go
func (s *Server) RegisterNamedVariableList(nvl NamedVariableList) error
```

RegisterNamedVariableList adds a static named variable list to the server's MMS object model. The list's domain (if domain-scoped) must already be registered via [Server.RegisterDomain](#func-server-registerdomain).

#### func (Server) RegisterVariable

```go
func (s *Server) RegisterVariable(v Variable) error
```

RegisterVariable adds a named variable to the server's MMS object model. The variable's domain (if domain-scoped) must already be registered. The TypeSpec is validated at registration time; unsupported type specifications are rejected early rather than at request time.

For association-scoped variables, use [ServerConn.RegisterVariable](#func-serverconn-registervariable) instead — association-scope variables are per-connection and cannot be registered on the shared server model.

#### func (Server) Serve

```go
func (s *Server) Serve(ctx context.Context, conn Transport) error
```

Serve handles a single MMS association over the provided transport. It performs the ISO handshake, then enters a request/response loop until the client concludes, releases or disconnects, or an error occurs. Serve returns nil after an orderly Conclude or Release.

The corresponding [ServerConn](#type-serverconn) is registered for the duration of Serve and can be obtained via [Server.Connections](#func-server-connections).

The caller owns the transport, with three exceptions in which Serve closes it to unblock a pending read: ctx is cancelled (Serve then returns an error matching ctx.Err()), the association is not established within [ServerOptions.AssociationTimeout](#func-serveroptions-associationtimeout), or [Server.Shutdown](#func-server-shutdown) aborts the association. [Server.ListenAndServe](#func-server-listenandserve) closes every accepted transport when its Serve returns.

Serve blocks until the connection is complete. For serving multiple connections, call Serve in a goroutine per accepted transport.

#### func (Server) SetVariableRead

```go
func (s *Server) SetVariableRead(domain, itemID string, fn func(context.Context) (*Value, error)) error
```

SetVariableRead replaces the read handler of a previously registered domain-scoped variable. This is intended for post-registration configuration, such as installing control-model-specific read handlers on CO attributes after the server model has been fully built.

Returns an error if no domain-scoped variable with the given domain and itemID exists.

#### func (Server) Shutdown

```go
func (s *Server) Shutdown(ctx context.Context) error
```

Shutdown stops the server gracefully: it closes the listeners of every running [Server.ListenAndServe](#func-server-listenandserve) (which then return ErrServerClosed), lets each association finish the request it is handling, and then aborts it (ACSE ABRT and transport close). MMS has no server-initiated orderly release, so idle associations are aborted right away.

If ctx is done before all in-flight requests finish, the remaining associations are aborted immediately and Shutdown returns ctx.Err(). After Shutdown, [Server.Serve](#func-server-serve) and [Server.ListenAndServe](#func-server-listenandserve) return ErrServerClosed. Shutdown is safe to call more than once.

### type ServerConn

```go
type ServerConn struct {

	// held while a confirmed request is handled

}
```

ServerConn represents an active server-side MMS association. It can be used to send unsolicited PDUs (e.g. InformationReport) to the connected client.

A ServerConn is valid for the duration of the [Server.Serve](#func-server-serve) call that created it. After Serve returns, the ServerConn is marked as closed and any subsequent [ServerConn.SendInformationReport](#func-serverconn-sendinformationreport) calls return ErrServerConnClosed.

#### func ServerConnFromContext

```go
func ServerConnFromContext(ctx context.Context) *ServerConn
```

ServerConnFromContext extracts the server-side connection from the request context. The connection is available in callbacks that receive a context from an active MMS service request (e.g. variable read/write handlers, write interceptors). Returns nil if no connection is present.

#### func (ServerConn) Abort

```go
func (sc *ServerConn) Abort(ctx context.Context) error
```

Abort sends a protocol-level MMS Abort PDU (ACSE ABRT wrapped in a Session ABORT SPDU) to the connected client and closes the connection. The send is best-effort: the connection is closed even if it fails. Returns ErrServerConnClosed if the connection was already closed.

#### func (ServerConn) AuthToken

```go
func (sc *ServerConn) AuthToken() any
```

AuthToken returns the opaque security token stored by the [Authenticator](#type-authenticator) during association establishment. Returns nil if no authenticator was configured or the authenticator did not set a token.

Upper layers (e.g. go-iec61850) use this to retrieve the principal or session context associated with the authenticated peer.

#### func (ServerConn) RegisterVariable

```go
func (sc *ServerConn) RegisterVariable(v Variable) error
```

RegisterVariable adds an association-scoped variable to this connection. Association-scope variables are visible only to this client and are automatically discarded when the connection closes.

This is typically called from an [Authenticator](#type-authenticator) or connection setup callback after the association is established. The variable is readable/writable via the standard MMS Read/Write services using ObjectScopeAssociation addressing.

#### func (ServerConn) SendInformationReport

```go
func (sc *ServerConn) SendInformationReport(ctx context.Context, req *InformationReportRequest) error
```

SendInformationReport sends an InformationReport to a specific connected client. Returns ErrServerConnClosed if the connection has been closed.

#### func (ServerConn) SendUnsolicitedStatus

```go
func (sc *ServerConn) SendUnsolicitedStatus(ctx context.Context, status ServerStatus) error
```

SendUnsolicitedStatus sends an UnsolicitedStatus unconfirmed PDU to the connected client. This provides the client with VMD status without a preceding Status request. Returns ErrServerConnClosed if the connection has been closed.

```go

	MMS ServerMMSOptions

	// Logger, when non-nil, enables structured MMS/server logging.
	// When nil (default), a discard handler is used. Does not configure
	// transport/iso logging — use iso.WithLogger on the listener
	// separately (see OBSERVABILITY.md).
	Logger *slog.Logger

	// Authenticate is called during association establishment to
	// accept or reject peers. If nil, all associations are accepted.

	// See [Authenticator] for callback semantics and examples.

	// FileProvider, if set, enables MMS file services (FileOpen,
	// FileRead, FileClose, FileDelete, FileDirectory). When nil,
	// file service requests are rejected with service-unsupported.

	// JournalProvider, if set, enables MMS journal services
	// (ReadJournal). When nil, journal service requests are
	// rejected with service-unsupported.

	// [Metrics]). Nil means no metrics.
```

### type Transport

```go
type Transport interface {
	Send(ctx context.Context, data []byte) error
	Receive(ctx context.Context) ([]byte, error)
	Close() error
}
```

Transport is an established COTP connection that can send and receive session-layer data. The transport/iso subpackage provides production implementations; test code typically uses mock transports.

Send transmits the raw session SPDU bytes as COTP user data. Receive blocks until data is available or the context is cancelled. Close closes the underlying connection.

### type TransportListener

```go
type TransportListener interface {
	Accept(ctx context.Context) (Transport, error)
	Close() error
	Addr() net.Addr
}
```

TransportListener accepts incoming connections and returns Transport instances ready for MMS server use. The production implementation lives in the transport/iso subpackage (iso.Listener).

### type TransportOptions

```go
type TransportOptions struct {
	LocalTSelector  []byte // calling T-selector (0xC1)
	RemoteTSelector []byte // called T-selector (0xC2)
}
```

TransportOptions configures the TPKT/COTP transport layer. It is read by transport/iso.Dial.

Each selector left nil is sent as 00 01; a non-nil empty slice omits it from the COTP CR. See transport/iso.WithCallingTSelector.

### type TypeSpec

```go
type TypeSpec struct {
	Type     ValueType
	Elements []TypeSpecElement // for Structure
	Count    int               // for Array: element count
	Element  *TypeSpec         // for Array: element type
	Size     int               // for Integer/Unsigned: bit width; for BitString/OctetString/VisibleString/MmsString: size

	// Float-specific fields (only valid when Type is ValueTypeFloat).
	FormatWidth   int // total float format width in bits (e.g. 32, 64)
	ExponentWidth int // exponent width in bits (e.g. 8 for IEEE 754 single)

	// TypeName holds the referenced ObjectName when the server returns
	// a typeName reference instead of an inline type definition.
	// Non-nil only when this TypeSpec represents a named type alias.
	TypeName *ObjectName
}
```

TypeSpec describes the MMS type of a variable. It is returned by [Client.GetVariableAccessAttributes](#func-client-getvariableaccessattributes) and used to register variables with [Server.RegisterVariable](#func-server-registervariable).

For scalar types, set Type and optionally Size (bit width for integers, length constraint for strings). For structures, populate Elements. For arrays, set Count and Element. For named type references, set Type to ValueTypeNamedType and TypeName to the referenced name.

Introspection helpers: [TypeSpec.ChildByName](#func-typespec-childbyname) and [TypeSpec.ChildByIndex](#func-typespec-childbyindex) navigate into structures and arrays. [TypeSpec.Resolve](#func-typespec-resolve) traverses a chain of [AccessSelector](#type-accessselector) values. [TypeSpec.DefaultValue](#func-typespec-defaultvalue) creates a zero-valued [Value](#type-value) matching the type. [TypeSpec.ShallowCompatible](#func-typespec-shallowcompatible) performs a quick pre-flight type check against a Value.

#### func (TypeSpec) ChildByIndex

```go
func (ts *TypeSpec) ChildByIndex(index int) (*TypeSpec, bool)
```

ChildByIndex returns the TypeSpec of a structure element or array element by index. For structures, the index maps to the element order. For arrays, the element type is returned regardless of index (as long as the index is within bounds).

#### func (TypeSpec) ChildByName

```go
func (ts *TypeSpec) ChildByName(name string) (*TypeSpec, bool)
```

ChildByName returns the TypeSpec of a structure element by name. Returns false if the TypeSpec is not a structure or the name is not found.

#### func (TypeSpec) DefaultValue

```go
func (ts *TypeSpec) DefaultValue() *Value
```

DefaultValue creates a zero-valued [Value](#type-value) matching this TypeSpec. For structures and arrays, all elements are recursively initialized. Returns nil for unsupported or named-type-reference specs.

For arrays, when Element is nil or Count is 0 the method returns an empty array (no elements). This is a deliberate best-effort placeholder: a non-zero Count with nil Element means the type spec is incomplete (the element type is unknown), so no elements can be initialized.

#### func (TypeSpec) Resolve

```go
func (ts *TypeSpec) Resolve(selectors ...AccessSelector) (*TypeSpec, error)
```

Resolve traverses the type tree using a chain of access selectors, returning the TypeSpec of the selected sub-element.

#### func (TypeSpec) ShallowCompatible

```go
func (ts *TypeSpec) ShallowCompatible(v *Value) bool
```

ShallowCompatible reports whether v has a top-level type and element count that matches ts. It checks only the outermost level — it does not recurse into array elements or structure components. Use this for quick pre-flight checks; it does not guarantee the value is deeply valid against the full type tree.

### type TypeSpecElement

```go
type TypeSpecElement struct {
	Name string
	Type TypeSpec
}
```

TypeSpecElement represents a single element within a structure type specification.

### type Value

```go
type Value struct {

	// Exactly one of these is populated based on typ.

	// OctetString, BitString
	// BitString: number of valid bits
	// VisibleString, MmsString

	// UTCTime quality byte (IEC 61850-8-1 TimeQuality)

	// Structure, Array

	// ObjectIdentifier arcs

}
```

Value represents an MMS typed data value.

Create values with the typed constructors:

	v := mms.NewInteger(42)
	v := mms.NewOctetString([]byte{0x01, 0x02})
	v := mms.NewArray([]*mms.Value{elem1, elem2})

Use [Value.Type](#func-value-type) to determine the kind, then call the corresponding accessor. Accessors return (T, bool) where the bool is false if the value's type does not match — this avoids panics for ordinary API misuse:

	i, ok := v.Int64()
	b, ok := v.OctetString()
	elems, ok := v.ArrayElements()

Byte slices and element slices are defensively copied by both constructors and accessors. Child [\*Value](#type-value) pointers within composite values (arrays, structures) are shared; use [Value.Clone](#func-value-clone) for a full deep copy. Use [Value.Get](#func-value-get) with selectors for nested access.

#### func NewArray

```go
func NewArray(elements []*Value) *Value
```

NewArray creates a [Value](#type-value) of type ValueTypeArray. The element slice is shallow-copied: the slice header is independent but the child [\*Value](#type-value) pointers are shared with the caller. Mutating a child value after construction is visible through both the original slice and this Value. Use [Value.Clone](#func-value-clone) if full ownership is needed.

#### func NewBCD

```go
func NewBCD(v int64) *Value
```

NewBCD creates a [Value](#type-value) of type ValueTypeBCD.

#### func NewBinaryTime

```go
func NewBinaryTime(ms int64) *Value
```

NewBinaryTime creates a [Value](#type-value) of type ValueTypeBinaryTime. The value is milliseconds since the Unix epoch. The MMS TimeOfDay encoding counts days from 1984-01-01 in 16 bits, so only instants from 1984-01-01 through 2163-06-05 can be sent in the dated (6-octet) form. Values from 0 to 86399999 (one day) are sent in the 4-octet form, which carries milliseconds since midnight without a date; a 4-octet TimeOfDay received from a peer decodes to such a value. Other values fail to encode.

#### func NewBitString

```go
func NewBitString(bits []byte) *Value
```

NewBitString creates a [Value](#type-value) of type ValueTypeBitString. All bits in the byte slice are considered valid (bitLen = len\*8).

#### func NewBitStringWithLength

```go
func NewBitStringWithLength(bits []byte, bitLen int) *Value
```

NewBitStringWithLength creates a [Value](#type-value) of type ValueTypeBitString with an explicit bit length. Use this when the number of valid bits is not a multiple of 8.

#### func NewBoolean

```go
func NewBoolean(b bool) *Value
```

NewBoolean creates a [Value](#type-value) of type ValueTypeBoolean.

#### func NewBooleanArray

```go
func NewBooleanArray(bits []byte, bitLen int) *Value
```

NewBooleanArray creates a [Value](#type-value) of type ValueTypeBooleanArray. The byte slice and bit length represent packed boolean values encoded as a BIT STRING. The slice is defensively copied.

#### func NewDataAccessError

```go
func NewDataAccessError(code DataAccessErrorCode) *Value
```

NewDataAccessError creates a [Value](#type-value) of type ValueTypeDataAccessError.

#### func NewFloat

```go
func NewFloat(f float64) *Value
```

NewFloat creates a [Value](#type-value) of type ValueTypeFloat.

#### func NewGeneralizedTime

```go
func NewGeneralizedTime(t time.Time) *Value
```

NewGeneralizedTime creates a [Value](#type-value) of type ValueTypeGeneralizedTime.

#### func NewInteger

```go
func NewInteger(i int64) *Value
```

NewInteger creates a [Value](#type-value) of type ValueTypeInteger.

#### func NewMmsString

```go
func NewMmsString(s string) *Value
```

NewMmsString creates a [Value](#type-value) of type ValueTypeMmsString. s must be valid UTF-8: MMSString is a UTF8String, so encoding anything else fails.

#### func NewObjectIdentifier

```go
func NewObjectIdentifier(oid []int) *Value
```

NewObjectIdentifier creates a [Value](#type-value) of type ValueTypeObjectIdentifier. The OID slice is defensively copied.

#### func NewOctetString

```go
func NewOctetString(data []byte) *Value
```

NewOctetString creates a [Value](#type-value) of type ValueTypeOctetString.

#### func NewReal

```go
func NewReal(f float64) *Value
```

NewReal creates a [Value](#type-value) of type ValueTypeReal. The value uses ASN.1 REAL encoding (ITU-T X.690 §8.5) on the wire, as opposed to MMS FloatingPoint encoding used by ValueTypeFloat.

#### func NewStructure

```go
func NewStructure(elements []*Value) *Value
```

NewStructure creates a [Value](#type-value) of type ValueTypeStructure. The element slice is shallow-copied: the slice header is independent but the child [\*Value](#type-value) pointers are shared with the caller. Mutating a child value after construction is visible through both the original slice and this Value. Use [Value.Clone](#func-value-clone) if full ownership is needed.

#### func NewUTCTime

```go
func NewUTCTime(t time.Time) *Value
```

NewUTCTime creates a [Value](#type-value) of type ValueTypeUTCTime with a default quality of 0x0a (10-bit sub-second accuracy), matching the libIEC61850 C reference default.

#### func NewUTCTimeWithQuality

```go
func NewUTCTimeWithQuality(t time.Time, quality uint8) *Value
```

NewUTCTimeWithQuality creates a [Value](#type-value) of type ValueTypeUTCTime with an explicit IEC 61850-8-1 TimeQuality byte. See UTCTimeQualityLeapSecondsKnown and related constants for bit definitions.

#### func NewUnsigned

```go
func NewUnsigned(u uint64) *Value
```

NewUnsigned creates a [Value](#type-value) of type ValueTypeUnsigned.

#### func NewVisibleString

```go
func NewVisibleString(s string) *Value
```

NewVisibleString creates a [Value](#type-value) of type ValueTypeVisibleString.

#### func (Value) ArrayElements

```go
func (v *Value) ArrayElements() (val []*Value, ok bool)
```

ArrayElements returns a shallow copy of the element slice of an array value. The returned slice is independent but the child [\*Value](#type-value) pointers are shared; mutating a child affects the original Value. ok is false if the value is not ValueTypeArray.

```go
func (v *Value) BCD() (val int64, ok bool)
```

BCD returns the BCD-encoded integer value. ok is false if the value is not ValueTypeBCD.

#### func (Value) BinaryTime

```go
func (v *Value) BinaryTime() (val int64, ok bool)
```

BinaryTime returns the binary time as milliseconds. ok is false if the value is not ValueTypeBinaryTime.

#### func (Value) BitString

```go
func (v *Value) BitString() (val []byte, ok bool)
```

BitString returns a copy of the bit string as a byte slice. ok is false if the value is not ValueTypeBitString.

#### func (Value) BitStringLength

```go
func (v *Value) BitStringLength() (val int, ok bool)
```

BitStringLength returns the number of valid bits in the bit string. ok is false if the value is not ValueTypeBitString.

#### func (Value) Bool

```go
func (v *Value) Bool() (val bool, ok bool)
```

Bool returns the boolean value. ok is false if the value is not ValueTypeBoolean.

#### func (Value) BooleanArray

```go

```

BooleanArray returns a copy of the packed boolean array as a byte slice and the number of valid bits. ok is false if the value is not ValueTypeBooleanArray.

#### func (Value) Clone

```go
func (v *Value) Clone() *Value
```

Clone returns a deep copy of the value, including all nested structure and array elements.

#### func (Value) DataAccessErr

```go
func (v *Value) DataAccessErr() (val DataAccessErrorCode, ok bool)
```

DataAccessErr returns the data access error code. ok is false if the value is not ValueTypeDataAccessError.

#### func (Value) Equal

```go
func (v *Value) Equal(other *Value) bool
```

Equal returns true if v and other have the same type and value, including deep comparison of structures and arrays. Float and Real values are compared exactly: bit for bit, except that every NaN equals every other NaN (so Equal is reflexive, and +0 differs from -0). If epsilon-based float equality is needed, callers should implement that separately.

#### func (Value) Float32

```go
func (v *Value) Float32() (val float32, ok bool)
```

Float32 returns a 32-bit float. ok is false if the value is not ValueTypeFloat.

#### func (Value) Float64

```go
func (v *Value) Float64() (val float64, ok bool)
```

Float64 returns a 64-bit float. ok is false if the value is not ValueTypeFloat.

#### func (Value) GeneralizedTime

```go
func (v *Value) GeneralizedTime() (val time.Time, ok bool)
```

GeneralizedTime returns the generalized timestamp. ok is false if the value is not ValueTypeGeneralizedTime.

#### func (Value) Get

```go
func (v *Value) Get(selectors ...AccessSelector) (*Value, error)
```

Get traverses nested structure/array values using a chain of access selectors. Returns the selected sub-value or an error if the path is invalid.

Note: Component selectors that use string names require the [TypeSpec](#type-typespec) to resolve component positions. Without a TypeSpec, use integer index selectors instead (see [SelectIndex](#func-selectindex)).

#### func (Value) Int32

```go
func (v *Value) Int32() (val int32, ok bool)
```

Int32 returns a signed 32-bit integer. ok is false if the value is not ValueTypeInteger or if the value overflows int32.

#### func (Value) Int64

```go
func (v *Value) Int64() (val int64, ok bool)
```

Int64 returns a signed 64-bit integer. ok is false if the value is not ValueTypeInteger.

#### func (Value) MmsString

```go
func (v *Value) MmsString() (val string, ok bool)
```

MmsString returns the MMS string. ok is false if the value is not ValueTypeMmsString.

```go
func (v *Value) ObjectIdentifier() (val []int, ok bool)
```

ObjectIdentifier returns a copy of the OID arcs. ok is false if the value is not ValueTypeObjectIdentifier.

#### func (Value) OctetString

```go

```

OctetString returns a copy of the octet string. ok is false if the value is not ValueTypeOctetString.

```go

```

#### func (Value) String

```go
func (v *Value) String() string
```

String returns a human-readable representation of the value for debugging and logging.

#### func (Value) Structure

```go
func (v *Value) Structure() (val []*Value, ok bool)
```

Structure returns a shallow copy of the element slice of a structure value. The returned slice is independent but the child [\*Value](#type-value) pointers are shared; mutating a child affects the original Value. ok is false if the value is not ValueTypeStructure.

#### func (Value) Type

```go
func (v *Value) Type() ValueType
```

Type returns the [ValueType](#type-valuetype) of this value.

#### func (Value) UTCTime

```go
func (v *Value) UTCTime() (val time.Time, ok bool)
```

UTCTime returns the UTC timestamp. ok is false if the value is not ValueTypeUTCTime.

#### func (Value) UTCTimeQuality

```go
func (v *Value) UTCTimeQuality() uint8
```

UTCTimeQuality returns the IEC 61850-8-1 TimeQuality byte for a ValueTypeUTCTime value. Returns 0 for non-UTCTime values.

Bit layout:

  - Bit 7 (0x80): Leap Seconds Known
  - Bit 6 (0x40): Clock Failure
  - Bit 5 (0x20): Clock Not Synchronized
  - Bits 0-4 (0x1F): Sub-second time accuracy (significant bits; 31 = unspecified)

#### func (Value) Uint32

```go
func (v *Value) Uint32() (val uint32, ok bool)
```

Uint32 returns an unsigned 32-bit integer. ok is false if the value is not ValueTypeUnsigned or if the value overflows uint32.

#### func (Value) Uint64

```go
func (v *Value) Uint64() (val uint64, ok bool)
```

Uint64 returns an unsigned 64-bit integer. ok is false if the value is not ValueTypeUnsigned.

#### func (Value) VisibleString

```go
func (v *Value) VisibleString() (val string, ok bool)
```

VisibleString returns the visible string. ok is false if the value is not ValueTypeVisibleString.

### type ValueType

```go
type ValueType int
```

ValueType identifies the type of data held in a [Value](#type-value).

```go
const (
	ValueTypeBoolean          ValueType = iota
	ValueTypeInteger                    // signed integer
	ValueTypeUnsigned                   // unsigned integer
	ValueTypeFloat                      // IEEE 754 floating point
	ValueTypeBitString                  // ordered sequence of bits
	ValueTypeOctetString                // arbitrary byte sequence
	ValueTypeVisibleString              // ISO 646 visible string
	ValueTypeMmsString                  // MMS string (UTF-8)
	ValueTypeUTCTime                    // UTC timestamp
	ValueTypeBinaryTime                 // binary-encoded time
	ValueTypeArray                      // ordered homogeneous collection
	ValueTypeStructure                  // ordered heterogeneous collection
	ValueTypeDataAccessError            // per-variable access error
	ValueTypeNamedType                  // reference to a named type alias (see TypeSpec.TypeName)
	ValueTypeGeneralizedTime            // ISO 8601 generalized time
	ValueTypeBCD                        // binary-coded decimal
	ValueTypeObjectIdentifier           // ASN.1 OBJECT IDENTIFIER
	ValueTypeReal                       // ASN.1 REAL (ITU-T X.690 §8.5 binary encoding)
	ValueTypeBooleanArray               // packed boolean array (BIT STRING)
)
```

#### func (ValueType) String

```go
func (t ValueType) String() string
```

String returns the human-readable name of the ValueType.

### type Variable

```go
type Variable struct {
	Name     ObjectName
	TypeSpec TypeSpec

	// Deletable reports whether the variable can be deleted.
	Deletable bool

	// Read is called when a client reads this variable. If nil, reads
	// return a data-access-error (object-access-denied).
	Read func(ctx context.Context) (*Value, error)

	// Write is called when a client writes this variable. If nil, writes
	// return a data-access-error (object-access-denied).
	Write func(ctx context.Context, v *Value) error
}
```

Variable describes a named MMS variable registered with a [Server](#type-server).

At minimum, Name and TypeSpec must be set. Read is required for the variable to be readable; Write is required for it to be writable.

### type VariableAccessAttributes

```go
type VariableAccessAttributes struct {
	Deletable bool
	TypeSpec  TypeSpec
}
```

VariableAccessAttributes holds the result of a GetVariableAccessAttributes operation.

### type VariableSpec

```go
type VariableSpec struct {
	Name            ObjectName
	AlternateAccess []AccessSelector
}
```

VariableSpec identifies a variable with optional sub-element selection via alternate access. Use this with [Client.ReadVariables](#func-client-readvariables) and [Client.WriteVariables](#func-client-writevariables) for component, index, or range access.

WriteAccessResult holds the per-variable outcome from a multi-variable write operation. Success is true when ErrorCode is zero.
